eMOLT Update 2026-09-25

Chlorophyll a concentrations documented by the PACE satellite from 9/23/2026. The red areas represent concentrations of over 20 mg per cubic meter

The noreaster coming this weekend will likely cause quite a bit of mixing along the coastline from Massachusetts up to Maine. Currently, there’s still a lot of algae in the water, but oxygen levels remain high at the stations eMOLT participants are monitoring around Casco Bay.

Thanks to Capt. John on the F/V Direction for flagging a dead link in last week’s email. The TimeZero compatible file of Bottom Trawl Stations should be back up on emolt.org now that we’ve dealt with an errant backslash.

This week, the eMOLT fleet recorded 201 tows of sensorized fishing gear totaling 4680 sensor hours underwater. Bottom temps are in line with last year’s averages most place except for Georges Bank, where temps are averaging ~4 degrees Fahrenheit warmer than they were at this time last year. This corresponds well to observations from a captain I spoke with in New Bedford earlier this week who said he’s seen well mixed temps in the mid 60s up on the bank.

FISHBOT bottom temperature records from the past week. The data are available on the Commercial Fisheries Research Foundation ERDDAP and an interactive visualization is available at the Cape Cod Ocean Watch dashboard hosted by Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution. FISHBOT aggregates data provided by participants in eMOLT, the CFRF Lobster and Jonah Crab Research Fleet, the CFRF Shelf Research Fleet, the Cape Cod Commercial Fishermen’s Alliance Cape Cod Oceanographic Research Fleet, the Maine Coast Fishermen’s Association Fisheries Ocean Data Program, MassDMF Cape Cod Bay Study Fleet, the Northeast Fisheries Science Center Study Fleet, and the Northeast Fisheries Science Center Ecosystem Monitoring Surveys

Dissolved Oxygen

Oxygen levels remain high off Stonington, ME and east of Nantucket Sound. Levels are lower, but still in the acceptable range in Casco Bay.

Without the Warden out and about and with fewer fishermen out this week, there’s not a lot of data to look at in this week’s screenshot from Massachusetts DMF’s Cape Cod Bay dashboard. You can see one low oxygen value off of Wellfleet. The other values north of the canal are good.
